citation: Schalk G, McFarland DJ, Hinterberger T, Birbaumer N, Wolpaw JR. BCI2000: a general-purpose brain-computer interface (BCI) system. IEEE Trans Biomed Eng 2004;51(6):1034-1043. EEG Motor Movement/Imagery Database, PhysioNet (Goldberger et al. 2000).
record_used: subject S002, baseline run R02 (eyes-closed), channel POz (posterior), first 10 s at 160 Hz (1600 samples) -- the SAME git-tracked vector the other EEG complexity cases use.
pipeline: readRDS(eeg_poz_s002r02) -> PhysioEEG::phaseEntropy(delay=1, k=4): form the Second-Order Difference Plot (first difference x(n+1)-x(n) vs second difference x(n+2)-x(n+1)), take each points polar angle (quadrant-corrected to [0,2pi)), bin into k sectors, and take the normalized Shannon entropy of the angle-weighted sector distribution. The reference re-computes it with NeuroKit2 entropy_phase across the sector count k, via reticulate. Deterministic.
note: The root is the POz channel numeric vector (shared with the other EEG complexity cases). Phase entropy (Rohila & Sharma 2019) is a phase-plane complexity measure from the Second-Order Difference Plot (SODP): it summarizes how the signals local rate-of-change (first difference) and change-of-rate (second difference) co-vary, by binning the SODP polar angle into k sectors and taking the normalized Shannon entropy of the angle-weighted distribution. phaseEntropy is a NEW op filling the phase-plane-geometry gap (the ecosystem had amplitude, template-matching and 1-D symbolic dispersion/increment/slope entropies but not the SODP entropy). It reproduces NeuroKit2 entropy_phase BIT-FOR-BIT (max |diff| ~4e-16) across the sector count k. On real eyes-closed POz EEG PhasEn increases with k (1.238 at k=4 -> 1.287 at k=6 -> 1.299 at k=8) and sits below the 1/ln2=1.443 normalization ceiling. HONEST: the normalization follows NeuroKit2 exactly (a base-2 Shannon term / natural-log ln(k)), so PhasEn ranges in [0, 1/ln2]; the value depends on (delay, k)=NeuroKit2 defaults; the reproducible content is the bit-exact family and the k-structure, not an absolute constant.
